previewNote.en: Local ONNX Runtime models (SQL Server 2025 on Windows) are in preview.

heading.en: Models, tokens and embeddings in one minute

body.en: An **embedding model** turns text (or images) into a vector of numbers so similar meanings get similar vectors. A **chat/completion model** (LLM) generates text. Models read **tokens** (word pieces), have **input limits** and are billed per token. In SQL Server 2025, Azure SQL Database, Azure SQL Managed Instance (Always-up-to-date) and SQL database in Fabric, an **external model** is a database object that stores *where* an embedding endpoint is, *how* to authenticate and *which* model to call, so T-SQL can run `AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS(text USE MODEL m)`. See the Foundations lesson on vectors for the basics.

Compare candidates on:
- **Modality**: text-only vs **multimodal** (text + images). Product photos or scanned documents need a multimodal embedding model.
- **Language support**: **multilingual** models embed different languages into the same space, so a Spanish query can match English content.
- **Size / dimensions**: larger models and more dimensions usually capture more nuance but cost more storage, memory, latency and money. `text-embedding-ada-002` and `text-embedding-3-small` return **1,536** dimensions; `text-embedding-3-large` returns **3,072**. The `text-embedding-3` models accept a **`dimensions`** parameter to shorten vectors.
- **Fit with the vector type**: `vector` float32 allows up to **1,998** dimensions and float16 up to **3,996**, so 3,072-dimension embeddings need float16 or a smaller `dimensions` value.
- **Token limits**: current Azure OpenAI embedding models accept up to **8,192 tokens per input** (up to 2,048 inputs per request), which drives your chunk size.
- **Structured output** (chat models): JSON Schema output (`response_format` type `json_schema`, `strict: true`, every property required, `additionalProperties: false`) makes responses easy to parse with `OPENJSON`/`JSON_VALUE` — useful in RAG.
- **Hosting & lifecycle**: Microsoft Foundry's model catalog shows capabilities, benchmarks, versions and retirement dates; local options (Ollama, ONNX Runtime) keep data on-premises.
**Rule:** the same embedding model (and dimensions) must be used for stored vectors *and* query vectors.

Steps: (1) make sure outbound REST calls are allowed (`external rest endpoint enabled` is on by default in Azure SQL Database and Fabric; enable it with `sp_configure` in SQL Server 2025), (2) create a **database master key**, (3) create a **database scoped credential** whose **name is the endpoint URL** (no query string), (4) `CREATE EXTERNAL MODEL`.
- `LOCATION`: HTTPS endpoint, e.g. `https://{endpoint}/openai/deployments/{deployment}/embeddings?api-version=...` for Azure OpenAI, `https://{server}/v1/embeddings` for OpenAI, `https://localhost:{port}/api/embed` for Ollama, or a local folder for ONNX Runtime.
- `API_FORMAT`: `Azure OpenAI`, `OpenAI`, `Ollama`, `ONNX Runtime`.
- `MODEL_TYPE`: `EMBEDDINGS` (the only accepted value).
- `MODEL`: model name. `CREDENTIAL`: the credential. `PARAMETERS`: JSON added to each request, e.g. `{"dimensions":1024}` or `{"sql_rest_options":{"retry_count":3}}` (0–10).
- Credentials: **Managed identity** (`IDENTITY = 'Managed Identity'`, `SECRET = '{"resourceid":"https://cognitiveservices.azure.com"}'`) — preferred; or an API key (`IDENTITY = 'HTTPEndpointHeaders'`, `SECRET = '{"api-key":"..."}'`). SQL Server 2025 needs Azure Arc and `allow server scoped db credentials` for managed identity.

- **Permissions**: `CREATE EXTERNAL MODEL` or `ALTER ANY EXTERNAL MODEL` to create/alter; users who call AI functions need `GRANT EXECUTE ON EXTERNAL MODEL::ProductEmbedder TO [app_user]`. `AUTHORIZATION owner` sets the owner.
- **Change** with `ALTER EXTERNAL MODEL m SET (MODEL = '...', LOCATION = '...', PARAMETERS = '...')`. **Remove** with `DROP EXTERNAL MODEL m` — blocked while a `SCHEMABINDING` view references it.
- **Inspect** with `sys.external_models`.
- **Override per call**: `AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS(text USE MODEL m PARAMETERS @json)` overrides model parameters (e.g., dimensions or retry_count) for that call.
- **Troubleshoot** with the `ai_generate_embeddings_summary` and `external_rest_endpoint_summary` extended events.
- **Switching models** changes the vector space: re-embed all stored rows (and recreate vector indexes) before querying with the new model.
- **Local ONNX Runtime** (SQL Server 2025 on Windows, preview): needs Machine Learning Services, `external AI runtimes enabled`, `PREVIEW_FEATURES`, and `LOCAL_RUNTIME_PATH`; only load models from trusted sources.

examTips.en: Evaluate models by modality, language support, size/dimensions, token limits, structured output and lifecycle.
ada-002 and 3-small = 1,536 dims; 3-large = 3,072; float32 vector max 1,998 → shorten with dimensions or use float16 (max 3,996).
CREATE EXTERNAL MODEL: LOCATION, API_FORMAT (Azure OpenAI/OpenAI/Ollama/ONNX Runtime), MODEL_TYPE = EMBEDDINGS, MODEL, CREDENTIAL, PARAMETERS.
Credential name = endpoint URL (no query string); managed identity preferred over API keys.
EXECUTE ON EXTERNAL MODEL::name lets a user call AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS; CREATE/ALTER ANY EXTERNAL MODEL to manage.
retry_count 0–10 in PARAMETERS ({"sql_rest_options":{"retry_count":n}}); call-level PARAMETERS override the model's.
Query and stored vectors must come from the same model; changing models means re-embedding.
